text: You scan the code, type your PIN, and in a couple of seconds, it's paid. But where did the money actually go?
Your payment app doesn't hold your money. It's a messenger, linked to a partner bank.
It sends your request to the U.P.I. switch, run by N.P.C.I., the exchange that connects hundreds of banks.
The switch asks your bank to check your PIN, which is encrypted so only your bank can read it, and your balance.
Then the switch tells the shop's bank to credit theirs.
Both apps get a confirmation. Done.
In September twenty twenty-six, this happened over twenty-four billion times. That's about eight hundred million payments, every single day.
All on a system launched in April twenty sixteen.
